fw_at_the_ramp_foot.description: I watch everything that comes up the ramp, because everything that reaches this city comes up it. I'm not a nervous man, and I've been nervous for a month. Galak outriders have started standing at the bottom, in daylight, in numbers, where the whole Landing can look down and count them. The Khan's Chosen are the ones with the standard, and their Wranglers hold the kodo back at Broadback, south-west of the ramp. Go down and make the ground in front of that ramp expensive, as far as Broadback.
fw_at_the_ramp_foot.accept_text: I'm not asking for a war. I want them standing somewhere I can't see from my own gate.
fw_at_the_ramp_foot.turn_in_text:
They've moved back half a mile, in good order, which I notice.

Nobody routed them, they chose to go. That's worse, and I'm going to tell the council so whether they want to hear it or not.

fw_clay_up_the_ramp.description: If you want to understand this city, stand at the bottom of the ramp for a day. My clay comes up it in sacks from a pit four days west, and every pot in Freewind is priced to match. There's clay in the salt pans at Saltwatch, south of the ramp foot, two days closer, and everyone's told me it won't fire, and nobody's tried. Dig me good sacks off the pans. Dig below the crust, because the crust is salt and salt ruins a pot, and under it there's grey clay I want to see.
fw_clay_up_the_ramp.accept_text: The things that live on those pans are made of the same salt. Don't let them put it on you.
fw_clay_up_the_ramp.turn_in_text:
It really fires! It's pale, and it rings higher than the western clay, and it'll crack in the cold if the cold ever comes.

Two days closer makes it a different city.

fw_feed_below.description: I keep every four-legged animal in the city on the Landing, because kodo won't cross a rope bridge, and they worked that out faster than we did. So the pens are up here and the feed is down there, and twice a season somebody has to go down and cut it. There's grass worth cutting in the wash beds, the only green on the whole floor, green because that's where the year's water went. The best of them are under the Seam, north-west of the ramp foot, where the elk graze them down. Take a blade down and bring back what you can carry.
fw_feed_below.accept_text: Watch for scorpids in the shade of the cut banks. They're in there because it's cool, and they won't move for you.
fw_feed_below.turn_in_text:
It smells like the plain. It doesn't taste like the plain, and the kodo know it, but they'll eat it.

Everything up here is a version of something we used to have.

fw_harpies_weave.description: I build better bows than my mother did, and I've never stopped being annoyed about why. I've spent a season watching harpy nests through a glass from the Windward top. They're woven, laid in courses like thatch, with a turn at the end of each course that I can't do and can't stop thinking about. Bring me the weave, a piece with the courses still in it, big enough that I can see where the turn goes. You'll have to kill the Sheerwing Harpies to get it, and no, I haven't found a way round that.
fw_harpies_weave.accept_text: Not a handful of feathers. I want the weave whole.
fw_harpies_weave.turn_in_text:
Look at this. That's a bowyer's knot, or near enough, and it's being tied by something everyone in this city calls an animal.

I won't say that out loud yet. I'd like to be sure first, which is more courtesy than most of them get.

fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.description: I price everything by the back that carried it up the ramp, and lately every back costs more because of what's standing at the bottom. I'm not interested in the philosophy. I've got a column for what the escort costs, and I'd like it to be a smaller number by the end of the season. The Galak Windcatchers sit high and see a caravan's dust an hour out, and the riders under the Khan's Chosen are formed up before the drivers know they've been seen. Take out the windcatchers and the Chosen, and my escort column halves.
fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.accept_text: Kill the windcatchers and the riders are guessing. Guessing riders are cheap riders.
fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.turn_in_text:
It's down a third already, and I'll take a third.

You'll hear Namka say we should be talking to them. She's probably right, but she isn't the one buying rope.

fw_light_caravans.description: I've complained about the ramp for three years, because the ramp is safe to complain about. The real problem is on my tally sheet. Every caravan that comes up arrives lighter than it left, by an amount too regular to be theft and too large to be spillage, and the drivers have stopped mentioning it. The road east runs between the Sisters, through a gap you have to go through, and that's where it happens. Go and stand in that gap, kill the Galak Outriders, and bring me their tally slips.
fw_light_caravans.accept_text: They write it down, and that's the part I can't get past. They aren't robbing us so much as invoicing us.
fw_light_caravans.turn_in_text:
It's itemised and dated, in a hand better than my clerk's.

I wanted to be angry about this, and now I've got to go and think about something else instead.

fw_older_than_the_wrong.description: I've spent three years looking for the dead of Thunder Bluff and not finding them, and I've found the one comfort to be had in not finding them. I've been out to Dryhollow twice. What's wrong with Dryhollow was wrong before the Integration, and it'll be wrong after, because not everything broken in this world was broken by Earth arriving. Go out to Dryhollow, south of the ramp beyond the salt pans, and stand in the middle of it for as long as you can manage. Then come back and tell me what you felt.
fw_older_than_the_wrong.accept_text: The Dryhollow Basilisks won't let you stand anywhere for long, so thin them first.
fw_older_than_the_wrong.turn_in_text:
You felt nothing? Then that's the answer.

Everywhere the Integration touched feels like a held breath. Dryhollow feels like a room nobody's been in. It's simply old, and I needed one thing in this country to be simply old.

fw_one_road_in.description: The single ramp is a better defence than Thunder Bluff ever had, and I know exactly what it means to say that. For two weeks something's been working the bottom of the ramp after dark, coming up far enough to be seen and then going back down, a little further every night. I'm nearly sure it's hyena, and nearly sure is why I'm sending somebody instead of going myself. Work the bottom of the ramp and the scrub on either side, kill the Dustmane Hyenas, and go out as far as the first bend of the Windward Road. If something's teaching them this ramp is worth walking up, I want to know whether it's a pack or a person.
fw_one_road_in.accept_text: Look at how they move as well as how many there are. A pack moves differently when someone's steering it.
fw_one_road_in.turn_in_text:
It was only a pack, then.

I'd rather it were hunger than somebody's idea. I can post a sentry against hunger.

fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.description: Every plank in this city came off a mountain that wasn't here three years ago, and I've been told that's the strange part. The bridges need relaying before the windy season, three spans, and the rope gets all the attention, because rope is frightening and decking isn't, which is exactly backwards. A deck board that splits is how somebody falls. Aspen takes a bend and holds it, and nothing that grew down here bends, which is why the bowyer's been insufferable lately. Mill me lengths at the bench, and bring up sound aspen bolts from the stacks in the Drowning Floor, the cave at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp.
fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.accept_text: The blind kodo bed down on the stacks. Mind them, and don't take the rotten bolts.
fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.turn_in_text:
That's good work, and dull work, and dull work is what a bridge is made of.

When somebody walks across that span and thinks about the rope, they're thinking about the wrong thing, and that's the compliment.

fw_the_anvil.description: I've got the highest standing ground in Thousand Needles, and a list of the four mesas nobody's ever been on top of. The Anvil is the nearest, the great flat rock at the far west end of the floor, past Needle's Eye. For eleven nights there's been a light up there that moves along the rim and goes out and comes back, and I've counted the pattern, and it doesn't repeat. Get round the base and as high as the scree will take you, close enough to see what's making that light. The Sheerwing Rooktenders come down to hunt at dusk, so take a few on the way.
fw_the_anvil.accept_text: I'm not asking you to climb the unclimbable. Just get close enough to see.
fw_the_anvil.turn_in_text:
So something's carrying the light along the rim and putting it down.

Then they're signalling. Then that's something they do, and I've been writing them up as weather for three years.

fw_the_drowned.description: I hold the names of everyone who was in Thunder Bluff when the ground took the city, in order, and I say them through once a season, which takes most of a night. Dral's told me what's down the hole at Broadback. There are things walking in it with salt set hard over them, and they have hands, and somebody somewhere has a list with their names on it. Bring back anything the saltbound shamblers carry that was made instead of grown, a notched stick, a ring, a tally. They're in the Drowning Floor, the cave at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp.
fw_the_drowned.accept_text: Whether you put them down out of mercy is yours to decide. I wouldn't argue with either answer.
fw_the_drowned.turn_in_text:
These are tally sticks, so they were salt crews, the ones who work the pans to the east and come back through the washes in the wet month.

Those are names I can find, and finding names is the only work I've ever been good at.

fw_the_glass_pan.description: I can tell you whether a thing came up out of the mesas or down off the mountain, but I can't always tell you what either one is, and I'm honest about that. A salt crew came back from the far side of Dryhollow talking about a pan fused to glass, a flat sheet of it with the sky in it, and they wouldn't go back. The glass pan is at the south edge of Dryhollow, south of the ramp and on past Saltwatch. Go and look at it, and bring me pieces off the edge. The crew told me something lives out there and is still making the glass.
fw_the_glass_pan.accept_text: Take your pieces off the rim, and don't go to the middle. Nothing I want is worth that.
fw_the_glass_pan.turn_in_text:
It's fused all the way through, not glazed, as if it went through a kiln the size of the hollow.

I'll put this on the shelf and label it honestly: came up out of the mesas, cause unknown, don't go to the middle.

fw_the_parley.description: I built this city, and I can't get used to having built something again. I've listened to the warden, the quartermaster and the clerk, I've read the fourth column in the Galak ledger, and I've reached a conclusion the council will hate. The Galak aren't raiding Freewind, they're charging it for a road they maintain, and nobody on either side has ever once said so out loud. This word goes to the gap at the Sisters, to whoever's standing there, and it goes into a hand. Don't stick it in the ground or leave it on a stone.
fw_the_parley.accept_text: Walk up with it held where they can see it, and don't draw anything. If that frightens you, you've understood.
fw_the_parley.turn_in_text:
They took it, and read it in front of you, and kept it?

Then we're talking. Three years, a dead road and a city in the air, and all it needed was somebody willing to walk up holding a piece of paper. I'll be a long time forgiving myself for those three years.

fw_the_road_is_open.description: I've got something I haven't had in three years, a road and somebody to talk to at both ends of it. The Galak will let a caravan through, the price is written down, and the thing at the bottom of the hole under Broadback is dead. There's nothing left between Camp Taurajo and this city except distance, and we've solved distance before. Take this north to Wrangler Tull at Camp Taurajo, all of it, the terms, the toll, the schedule, and the Galak's own hand at the bottom. That mark took longer to get than the rest put together.
fw_the_road_is_open.accept_text: Tull asked whether kodo could go down. Tell him yes, tell him what it costs, and watch his face.
fw_the_road_is_open.turn_in_text:
It's signed by a centaur. There's a centaur's mark on a tauren document, and somebody expects me to read it out at the corral gate.

I drove that road for twenty years and never once paid a toll on it. I also never once had to ask who kept it up. All right, then, we'll pay.

fw_the_spill.description: On a clear day I can see the dark line of the aspen along the north, and three years ago that line was sky. Things have been coming down it, mostly elk, walking south until the timber ran out and finding red hardpan and forty degrees of heat. They can't find the pass again, and the cats came after them and are doing no better. I'm not asking you to cull them, and I wouldn't call it that. Kill the Sunstruck Elk and the Downslope Lynx on the Seam, and finish what the sun has started.
fw_the_spill.accept_text: Get close enough that it's quick. That's the whole task, and I'm sorry it's one.
fw_the_spill.turn_in_text:
You'll have seen the ribs on them.

We came down a pass too. The difference is that we knew what we were walking into, and we still argue about whether that was better.

fw_toll_ledger.description: I write down everything that crosses this top, and it isn't suspicion. It's that we lost a city once without a list of what was in it. Bohl brought me a handful of Galak tally slips, and I haven't slept properly since, because they're better kept than mine, with a running balance and a fourth column I can't identify. I need more, and I don't mean slips. I need leaves out of the book the slips come from, and you'll find those on whoever's senior in a toll party.
fw_toll_ledger.accept_text: If they're keeping a balance against us, I want to know what for before the council decides for me.
fw_toll_ledger.turn_in_text:
It's a running total, against the road. They're charging us for the road itself, and they've been maintaining it.

There's a column for the upkeep too.

fw_where_the_water_goes.description: I know where everything that came up the ramp this season is, and I'll tell you to stop asking about anything that didn't. What I can't account for is water. Thousand Needles floods once a year, hard, and then it's dry for twelve months, and that much water doesn't evaporate, it goes somewhere. At the foot of Broadback there's a wash that runs in and doesn't run out. Go and stand at the mouth of it and look down.
fw_where_the_water_goes.accept_text: The Saltpan Kodo shelter in its mouth. Clear enough of them to get a proper look.
fw_where_the_water_goes.turn_in_text:
There was no bottom to it that you could see? A year's water, every year, into a hole with no bottom.

I've got a column in my book for things that go out and don't come back, and I'm going to need a bigger column.

fw_wrong_climate.description: I treat falls, mostly, off ladders more than off edges. Lately I've been treating drivers coming up the ramp with heat sickness in a season they've worked their whole lives. I think the floor is getting hotter, and I'd like to be wrong. An animal that starves and an animal that cooks don't leave the same marrow. Bring me marrow from the elk dying on the Seam, and a scrape of the ground they're dying on.
fw_wrong_climate.accept_text: If it's the heat, I'll have to go and tell Namka the floor is changing under a city that can't move.
fw_wrong_climate.turn_in_text:
It's the heat, not hunger.

I wanted it to be hunger. Hunger would have meant they were simply in the wrong place, and this means the place is going wrong.

fw_yearmaw.description: I've stopped keeping a column for the hole at Broadback and started keeping a page. The salt crews tell each other a story they don't tell outsiders, about something in the standing water at the bottom that waits all year for the flood. When the cave fills, everything in it drowns at once, and the thing in the sump has its one meal. The flood is four months out, so it's as hungry as it ever gets. It's in the lowest bay of the Drowning Floor, at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp, and the crews call it Yearmaw.
fw_yearmaw.accept_text: It has no eyes, and three of my drivers told me it waits until you move.
fw_yearmaw.turn_in_text:
So the crews were right, and I've been filing their story under rumour for two years.

There's a page in my book for that too. I'm going to go and change it, and make a note of who told me first.
